newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries end up as PPI suggests low inflation.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries end up as PPI suggests low inflation.

text.p: The prices of U.S. Treasury securities closed higher on Friday as the producer price index (PPI) continued to show inflation remained contained at the manufacturing level.

The Labor Department reported that producer prices fell 0.3 percent, and minus the volatile food energy components, also was off 0.3 percent in May. Economists had expected a modest gain of 0.1 percent in the index. The report was further evidence that inflation was subdued and the Federal Reserve could refrain from further tightening of monetary policy at its next meeting.

"The market has got a lot going for it with uncertainty overseas. The inflation news has been wonderful, but that should have been expected," said James Glassman, senior economist at Chase Securities Inc.
He said investors now saw the Federal Reserve refraining from further tightening until late summer or the fall. Glassman said another tightening in August even was questionable.
Glassman said there had been some statistical aberrations but the U.S. economy has been benefitting from the dollar's strength and high unemployment rates in Europe.
"Investors are coming here. Everything's working here to keep prices in check," Glassman said of the U.S. economy.

"We've got an environment in which inflation is better than expected. We've seen declining prices for five months in a row at the wholesale level," said Richard Berner, executive vice president and chief economist at Mellon Bank Corp.

In addition, higher yields on Treasuries than in overseas government bond markets were supporting the market, he said. Capital inflows from foreign investors were underpinning the prices of U.S. bonds, he said.
Berner saw the Fed abstaining from further tightening not only in July, but perhaps until its meeting in late September.
"There are no major imbalances in the economy. This might be described as a golden age," he said, and the current recovery could last for some time despite its long duration.
There was a danger of excessive balances building up in the financial markets as Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan has warned, Berner said.
"But we haven't seen asset price inflation translate into inflation as we traditionally characterized it," he added.

"Clearly the PPI news was another favorable development from the Treasury market's perspective," said Richard Rippe, chief economist at Prudential Securities Inc. "Inflationary pressures, at least at the wholesale level, have been virtually nonexistent," he said.
"We now have a picture of an economy slowing, the question is whether the slowdown seen in the second quarter will be superceded by more growth," Rippe said.
He saw the Fed remaining on hold in July -- even given worries of the economy strengthening again and the tight labor market.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond ended at 98-20/32, up 18/32, yielding 6.73 percent.

Two-year notes ended at 100-13/32, up 3/32 to yield 6.03 percent. Five-year notes rose 7/32 to 100-26/32 to yield 6.31 percent and the 10-year note was up 13/32 to 101-12/32, its yield at 6.43 percent.
Three-month bill rates rose one basis point to 4.84 percent, six-month rates were down two basis points at 5.12 percent and year bill rates were off three basis points at 5.33 percent.
